Haldane's pub quip ('two brothers or eight cousins'); W.D. Hamilton's Waterloo Station derivation, Nature rejection, 1963 Am Nat & 1964 J Theor Biol I/II (PMID 5875341, 5875340: rB > C & haplodiploid r = 0.75) refined by Hughes et al.'s 267-species ancestral-monogamy proof (2008 Science, PMID 18511689); George R. Price's 1970 Nature covariance equation (PMID 5428476) & 1972 multilevel extension (PMID 5073694), Maynard Smith & Price 1973 ESS, Frank (1995/2012, PMID 7475081, 22487312) & Price's heartbreaking Christian conversion and 1975 London death; Nowak, Tarnita & Wilson (2010, PMID 20740005) vs. the 137-author rebuttal by Abbot et al. teenKit.tldr: Charles Darwin was haunted by sterile worker bees that die defending their hive instead of having kids. W.D. Hamilton solved this by proving evolution cares about shared genes, not just personal survival ($rB > C$).
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding kin selection and cooperation reveals the deep mathematical roots of why humans and animals sacrifice their own comfort—or lives—to help family and society.
keyTakeaways: Natural selection normally rewards individuals who pass on their own genes, making self-sacrificing altruism look like an evolutionary trap.
Hamilton's Rule ($rB > C$) proves that altruism makes mathematical sense if the genetic benefit to your relatives ($rB$) outweighs the cost to you ($C$).
Extreme self-sacrifice is heavily driven by shared genetics, whether it's worker bees defending a hive or yeast cells sticking together via molecular 'green-beard' proteins.

vocab.meaning: Behavior of an animal that benefits another at its own expense or risk.
Natural selection in favor of behavior that maximizes the survival of close relatives sharing common genes.
A sex-determination system where males develop from unfertilized eggs and females from fertilized eggs, making sisters unusually genetically related.
A thought experiment and real molecular mechanism where a gene causes individuals to recognize and help other individuals who carry the exact same gene.

quiz.question: What was Darwin's ultimate evolutionary nightmare regarding honeybees?
options: They make honey too efficiently for other insects.
Worker bees give up reproducing entirely to die defending a hive they don't parent.
They mutate into entirely different species every winter.
They refuse to pollinate flowers native to South America.
quiz.explanation: Darwin was puzzled because natural selection favors individuals who pass on their own traits, yet sterile worker bees sacrifice their lives without ever having offspring.

quiz.question: In Hamilton's famous equation $rB > C$, what does the letter 'r' represent?
options: The rate of reproduction in a collapsing ecosystem
The physical radius of the animal's territory
The genetic relatedness between the altruist and the recipient
The total resistance of a gene to environmental mutations
quiz.explanation: The 'r' stands for the coefficient of relatedness, measuring the statistical probability that two individuals share the same gene.

quiz.question: J.B.S. Haldane famously quipped that he would gladly lay down his life for what specific group of relatives?
quiz.explanation: Because brothers share about 50% of your genes ($r=1/2$) and cousins share about 12.5% ($r=1/8$), mathematically saving two brothers equals saving eight cousins in terms of genetic survival.
